source.title: Policy Invariance Under Reward Transformations: Theory and Application to Reward Shaping
source.venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 1999), pp. 278-287

confidence_rationale: Foundational theorem with a necessary-and-sufficient, dynamics-independent guarantee -- exceptionally high source quality. It is the formal tethering constraint Strand B needs: it tells you EXACTLY which proxy signals provably do not distort the true goal. Direction is 'mixed' relative to a naive proxy-goal claim: it supports the usefulness of intermediate signals while proving that an arbitrary proxy (non-potential-based) can change the optimal policy. Mapping fidelity capped because REE's proxy is a learned, non-stationary, possibly affective signal, not a stationary state-only potential.
failure_signatures: Invariance holds only for an additive, Markov, state-only potential Phi(s) under fixed discount; action-dependent, history-dependent, or drifting (learned online) potentials break the guarantee unless specially handled.

Necessity: if a shaping reward is NOT potential-based, there EXIST dynamics and a base reward under which the optimal policy of the shaped problem differs from the true one -- i.e. an untethered proxy can provably divert the agent from the true goal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A shaping reward F(s,a,s') added to the environment reward preserves the set of optimal policies IF AND ONLY IF it is potential-based, F(s,a,s') = gamma*Phi(s') - Phi(s); this holds with no assumptions on transition dynamics or base reward.
mapping.ree_translation: REE's proxy/progress signals (the very thing that maintains a goal) carry a divergence risk: an intermediate signal that is NOT of the potential-difference form can pull behaviour away from the superordinate goal it was meant to serve. This grounds a prospective `proxy_tethering_guard` candidate -- the constraint that REE's maintenance proxy must approximate a potential difference over goal-proximity to stay aligned with INV-065's proxy goals rather than supplant them.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The theorem assumes a stationary, additive, state-only potential under a fixed objective. REE's maintenance proxy is learned, non-stationary, and affectively modulated, so the guarantee transfers only as a design target / limiting case, not as an off-the-shelf certificate. It also says nothing about WHICH potential to pick or about sample efficiency.
mapping.source_context: Reinforcement learning theory (MDPs); grid-world and continuous control applications.

confidence_components.notes: Theorem-grade source. The potential-based form is precisely the tethering constraint; transfer risk from REE's non-stationary learned proxy violating the stationarity assumption.
